intro.title: Open-mindedness
paragraphs: Your dream is to become a successful entrepreneur and create a business that brings people together.

You have just been hired by a large multinational company, where people from different cultures, backgrounds, and professions work together. Working at this company is a learning experience for you, as by completing various challenges within it, you will acquire the 30 skills included in the POMEIL Competency Map, which are essential for every entrepreneur.

Today, in the cafeteria, you'll meet Karina from Product Development and her colleague Daniel. Together they'll guide you through what it really means to stay open to new ideas — even when they challenge your own.

dialogues.introduction: Hey (username), nice to meet you! I'm the Product Development Lead, and I truly love working here. I've only just started, but I already feel like I need a new approach. All my life I've relied only on myself, so it's not easy for me to learn how to listen to someone else's ideas — especially while living in a new country. Daniel is helping me develop a selling strategy.
dialogues.introduction_part2: Somewhere in this room, there is a list with some useful tips regarding open-mindedness. Try to find it and read it carefully, then come back to me. Start by checking the coffee machine area.
dialogues.noteFound: Well done, you found the action plan!
dialogues.noteFound_part2: Open-mindedness means being aware of your own views while staying willing to understand the ideas and perspectives of others. It requires more than simply listening — it involves a genuine effort to appreciate different opinions and consider new information with respect. Open-mindedness helps reduce misunderstandings, challenges personal biases, and supports better communication with the people around you.

quiz.title: Open-Mindedness quiz - True or False

questions.text: Being open-minded means I must agree with every idea I hear.
questions.hint: Open-mindedness is about learning, not agreeing with everything.

questions.text: Listening to different opinions can help me understand situations better.
questions.hint: Ask yourself: does hearing more viewpoints give me more information or less?

questions.text: If an idea feels new or uncomfortable, I should reject it immediately.
questions.hint: Does open-mindedness happen when we close the door quickly, or when we stay curious?

quizComplete.title: Correct!
quizComplete.message: Excellent work! You've completed the first step in your open-mindedness training.

puzzleTwo.title: Open-Mindedness Quiz – Multiple Choice
puzzleTwo.question: What is the best way to show open-mindedness during a discussion?

options.b: Pay attention to others' viewpoints and ask curious questions
options.c: Ignore ideas that feel new or uncomfortable
options.d: Interrupt to explain why your idea is better

optionLabels.a: a) Decide your opinion before listening
optionLabels.b: b) Pay attention to others' viewpoints and ask curious questions
optionLabels.c: c) Ignore ideas that feel new or uncomfortable
optionLabels.d: d) Interrupt to explain why your idea is better

puzzleTwo.hint: Think about which answer shows curiosity and willingness to understand others, instead of shutting their ideas down.
puzzleTwo.answerOverlay:
After 3 attempts, here's the answer:

Question: When someone shares an idea you disagree with, what's the most open-minded response?

Options:
a) Immediately explain why you think they're wrong
b) Ask questions to understand their perspective better
c) Change the subject to avoid conflict
d) Agree with them to keep the peace

Correct Answer: b) Ask questions to understand their perspective better

Explanation: Open-mindedness is about showing curiosity and willingness to understand others, instead of shutting their ideas down. Asking questions helps you learn and shows respect for the other person's viewpoint.

puzzleThree.title: Open-mindedness quiz- Sequence ordering
puzzleThree.question: Place the following actions in the most open-minded order.
puzzleThree.placeholderText: Click steps on the left to add them here.

options.a: Ask a curious question to understand the person's perspective
options.b: Avoid judging or reacting too quickly
options.c: Listen openly to what the person is saying
options.d: Reflect briefly on what you heard before sharing your own view

hints.position1: An open-minded person always begins by truly listening — that creates ease for both sides.
hints.position2: After listening, keep your mind open by avoiding fast judgments.
hints.position3: Once the conversation feels calm and open-minded, you can ask curious questions to understand better.
hints.position4: After that, it becomes easy to share your own view respectfully.

puzzleThree.answerOverlay:
After 3 attempts, here's the answer:

Question: What is the correct sequence for practicing open-mindedness during a discussion?

Correct Answer:
1. "Listen openly to what the person is saying" (c) - An open-minded person always begins by truly listening, which creates ease for both sides and allows you to actually understand their perspective
2. "Avoid judging or reacting too quickly" (b) - Keep your mind open by avoiding fast judgments that could shut down the conversation or create tension
3. "Ask a curious question to understand the person's perspective" (a) - Once the conversation feels calm and open-minded, ask curious questions to understand better without putting them on the spot
4. "Reflect briefly on what you heard before sharing your own view" (d) - After listening and understanding, it becomes easy to share your own view respectfully

This sequence demonstrates true open-mindedness by prioritizing understanding before responding.

note.altText: A printed action plan with open-mindedness tips.

facts.strong: Your brain actually likes new ideas.
facts.text: When you hear a new perspective, your brain releases a tiny boost of dopamine — the same chemical linked to curiosity and learning. Open-mindedness literally feels good inside your head!
Studies show that when people realize they were wrong about something, their brain forms stronger learning connections. So making mistakes isn't embarrassing — it's an upgrade for your mind.
Curiosity turns a stressful disagreement into a puzzle. Instead of arguing, your brain switches into "explore mode," which lowers tension and improves problem-solving.

facts.strong: Trying new things makes your brain more flexible.
facts.text: Even small changes — like taking a new route home or tasting a food you usually skip — help your brain become more adaptable. That flexibility supports bigger open-minded thinking later.

facts.strong: Open-minded people make decisions faster, not slower.
facts.text: Surprisingly, people who hear different viewpoints often reach solutions quicker, because they see more options, avoid stubborn blocks, and adjust more easily
